## Appearance

Gilbert Blythe is a tall, handsome boy with broad shoulders, curly brown hair, and roguish hazel eyes. He is frank-faced with clear, straightforward eyes and often wears a teasing smile on his mouth.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050)_

## Personality

Gilbert is a clever and good-natured young man who is popular wherever he goes. He possesses his own thoughts about things alongside a strong determination to get the best out of life and put the best into it. Gracious in defeat, he maintains a well-intentioned spirit even in academic rivalries. Driven by his ambitions, he aims to earn his own way through college and has set his sights on becoming a doctor.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Queen’s P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. ## History

Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta with his sick father and spent a summer visiting cousins in [New Brunswick](../codex/places.md#new-brunswick) before returning home. During his time at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) schoolhouse, he attempted to get Anne's attention by pulling her hair and calling her "Carrots," prompting [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to smash a slate over his head and refuse his contrite apology. Though the two engaged in an intense academic rivalry, Gilbert later rescued [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) in a dory when her boat sank during a theatrical re-enactment, only for [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to coldly reject his friendship once more. When [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) took the Queen's entrance exams, Gilbert gained the medal while [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) won the Avery scholarship. Upon graduation, Gilbert gave up his secured position as the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school teacher so that [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) could remain close to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), leading the two to finally reconcile and become close friends. As they began their respective teaching careers, Gilbert actively collaborated with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) in the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers) and discussed their ambitions during frequent walks and meetings. Later, after [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) decided to leave teaching to attend [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college), Gilbert waited with her at [Echo Lodge](../codex/places.md#echo-lodge) following a wedding, where a quiet moment sparked a shift in how [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) perceived him and her own maturity.

## Quotes

> "It wasn’t particularly good of me at all, Anne. I was pleased to be able to do you some small service. Are we going to be friends after this? Have you really forgiven me my old fault?"
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P52](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0052)

> "We were born to be good friends, Anne. You’ve thwarted destiny enough. I know we can help each other in many ways. You are going to keep up your studies, aren’t you? So am I. Come, I’m going to walk home with you."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P55](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0055)

> “Not she,” said Gilbert emphatically. “I know Louisa Spencer well. She doesn’t ‘believe’ in Village Improvement Societies, but she does believe in dollars and cents. She’d be more likely to urge Judson on than to dissuade him.”
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P46](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0046)

> "Well, I must run up to MacPhersons’. Moody Spurgeon came home from Queen’s today for Sunday and he was to bring me out a book Professor Boyd is lending me."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P19](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0019)

> “I’m awfully sorry I made fun of your hair, Anne,” he whispered contritely. “Honest I am. Don’t be mad for keeps, now.”
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P49](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0049)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--gilbert-blythe.md)

Gilbert's connection with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) begins as a tense feud after he pulls her hair and calls her "Carrots," prompting [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to break a slate over his head and refuse his apology. Although they spend time as fierce academic rivals in school, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) eventually cold-shoulders him when he rescues her from a sinking boat pile. Over time, their relationship evolves into a close friendship and collaboration, developing into a mutual romantic interest.
